item.title: Steptoe and Son – British Comedy Radio
item.description: Steptoe and Son is a British sitcom written by Galton and Simpson about two rag and bone men living in Oil Drum Lane, a fictional street in Shepherd's Bush, London.

item.title: Les Dawson – British Comedy Radio
item.description: Leslie “Les” Dawson was an extremely popular English comedian remembered for his deadpan style, curmudgeonly persona and jokes about his mother-in-law and wife. item.title: Dad's Army Radio Show – British Comedy Radio
item.description: “Dad’s Army” was a long running British comedy series created and written by Jimmy Perry and David Croft. item.title: Parsley Sidings – British Comedy Radio
item.description: Parsley Sidings was a BBC Radio sitcom created by Jim Eldridge. It starred Arthur Lowe and Ian Lavender (who were also starring in the television wartime sitcom Dad’s Army at that time), together with Kenneth Connor from the Carry On films. item.title: Tony Hancock - Hancock's Half Hour – British Comedy Radio
item.description: Hancock's Half Hour was a BBC radio comedy / television series of the 50s starring Tony Hancock, Sid James, Hattie Jacques, Bill Kerr and Kenneth Williams.

item.title: The Clitheroe Kid - Jimmy Clitheroe – British Comedy Radio
item.description: The Clitheroe Kid was a BBC radio comedy show, featuring Northern comedian James Robinson ("Jimmy") Clitheroe in the role of a cheeky schoolboy.

item.title: Beyond Our Ken – British Comedy Radio
item.description: Beyond Our Ken featured characters similar to those later featured in Round the Horne, for instance, Betty Marsden’s Fanny Haddock (which parodied Fanny Cradock). It was also notable for Pertwee’s Frankie Howerd impersonation, Hankie Flowered, and Hugh Paddick’s working-class pop singer Ricky Livid – the name being a mickey-take on contemporary pop singers’ stage names...

item.title: Ken Dodd – British Comedy Radio
item.description: Sir Kenneth Arthur Dodd OBE (8 November 1927 – 11 March 2018) was a British comedian and singer-songwriter, famous for his frizzy hair or “fluff dom” and buck teeth or “denchers”, his favourite cleaner, the feather duster (or “tickling stick”) and his greeting “How tickled I am!”, as well as his send-off “Lots and Lots of Happiness!”....

item.title: On the Buses - TV Comedy – British Comedy Radio
item.description: On the Buses was broadcast on ITV from 1969 to 1973. Stan Butler played by Reg Varney was the cheeky bus driver in this classic LWT sitcom.
